For others stumbling on this report. This is a recent regression in AMD drivers. Please report the issue directly to AMD as well as they are the ones who need to fix it. 

As a workaround you can either roll back your driver to the last version, or switch to the D3D12 backend. You can switch to the D3D12 backend by going into your project settings and setting [`rendering/rendering_device/driver`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/classes/class_projectsettings.html#class-projectsettings-property-rendering-rendering-device-driver) to "d3d12"

I've looked around and seen some noise about this issue but none of the outcomes from that seem to be documented properly on this ticket. Unfortunately the driver team can't really progress with this until we're sure that it's 100% valid Vulkan API usage. This means we need a basic sample project that reproduces the issue and output from Vulkan validation layers showing there aren't any issues.

I suspect that getting a basic sample project that reproduces the issue is the easy part, but I fear that enabling Vulkan validation layers is the harder part that isn't easily exposed to Godot users/game developers. Is this easy to enable?

I also have invisible mesh issues since driver update and on more heavier scenes total corruption. (FLICKER WARNING)
<video src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d6df91b3-b843-4d0b-83bd-fbe0d519ef6b" controls preload></video>

> but I fear that enabling Vulkan validation layers is the harder part that isn't easily exposed to Godot users/game developers. Is this easy to enable?

Running a project with `--path /path/to/project/folder --gpu-validation` should do the trick. `--gpu-validation` works with any engine build, including official editor builds and debug/release export templates. For an exported project, run its executable with `--gpu-validation` alone.

You will need the Vulkan SDK installed for validation layers to be present.

Also consider `--gpu-abort`, which stops the process if a validation error comes up (both `--gpu-validation` and `--gpu-abort` should be used together in this case). However, `--gpu-abort` requires an editor or debug export template build to work (it won't work in release export template builds).

MRP: https://files.godot.foundation/s/JEKC3a7MkBgm4Ws

This is a simple example, it is just drawing a single cube mesh, but it still breaks.

The issue appears to be caused by AMD adrenaline software version 25.8.1 (Driver Version 25.10.25.01). As you can see above, it causes meshes to explode. Several versions of Godot are impacted, including several stable releases that have had no issues for months or years.

We have confirmed that there are no Vulkan Validation Layer Errors in the MRP. 

We have analyzed the issue a bit in Renderdoc and confirm the following:
1. The inputs to the shader appear fine (uniforms, vertex input, etc.)
2. The output of the vertex shader is totally broken (seemingly random numbers)
3. Removing chunks of the vertex shader code can make the shader behave properly. It appears to be a compiler issue since it gets triggered at random (for example after removing much of the shader code to fix the output, we can break things again by multiplying a mat4 by a mat4 identity matrix)

This issue only affects AMD, and it only affects Windows with Vulkan. Windows with D3D12 appears to be working fine.
Excellent stuff. I've forwarded it on. Thanks! @clayjohn

In case if someone else stuck or looking for workaround on AMD. In my case, switching `render` to `compatibility` configuration allows the project to continue functioning :)

Config `project.godot`
```
[rendering]

renderer/rendering_method="gl_compatibility"
rendering/rendering_device/fallback_to_d3d12=true
```

Given what we found, it seems to be exclusively a shader compilation issue of the particular shader that we are using. There was not one clear reason I could find as to what triggered it since it'd need deeper dives into AMD's GPU code generation, but I think building a test out of it would be very difficult and it just seems like a bug triggered by a particular combination of steps on the resulting SPIR-V. We'd have a very hard time proposing a test without knowing the specifics of the bug or if it even warrants a test for it.
